h: Suprasellar mass compressing the pituitary stalk: which hormone rises?
p: Stalk compression cuts off hypothalamic dopamine, which normally inhibits prolactin, so prolactin rises while the other anterior pituitary hormones fall.

h: Asthma diagnosis: inhaled agent causing a 20% FEV1 drop?
p: The methacholine challenge uses a cholinergic bronchoconstrictor; a 20% fall in FEV1 (PC20) confirms airway hyperreactivity. Albuterol and epinephrine are bronchodilators.

h: Mammogram, colonoscopy and Pap smear in an asymptomatic adult: level of prevention?
p: Secondary prevention detects disease early in the asymptomatic stage (screening). Primary prevents disease (vaccines); tertiary limits complications of established disease.

h: Eccentric behavior, chorea and memory loss, father affected younger: diagnosis?
p: Autosomal dominant CAG repeat expansion on chromosome 4 with anticipation (earlier onset in later generations); caudate atrophy.

h: Carbamazepine in pregnancy: classic birth defect?
p: Carbamazepine (like valproate) raises neural tube defect risk; give folic acid. Ebstein anomaly is linked to lithium and tooth discoloration to tetracyclines.

h: Repeated ED visits for opioids, no organic cause, external gain: diagnosis?
p: Malingering is consciously feigned illness for an external reward (here narcotics). Munchausen (factitious disorder) seeks the sick role, with no external gain.

h: Tall, upward lens dislocation, diastolic murmur: defective protein?
p: Marfan syndrome: FBN1 mutation. Ectopia lentis (superotemporal), aortic root dilation with aortic regurgitation, arachnodactyly.

h: Osteoporosis with hypertension: which antihypertensive helps bone?
p: Thiazides decrease urinary calcium excretion and may reduce fracture risk. Loop diuretics increase calcium loss.

h: Mycophenolate mofetil: mechanism of action?
p: It blocks IMPDH, depleting guanine nucleotides and so halting T and B cell proliferation. Used in lupus nephritis and transplant.

h: Antiretroviral NRTI classically causing pancreatitis?
p: Didanosine causes pancreatitis and peripheral neuropathy. Zidovudine causes bone marrow suppression (anemia); efavirenz causes CNS effects and vivid dreams.

h: Cape-like pain and temperature loss in both arms, vibration spared: tract affected?
p: A syrinx (syringomyelia) interrupts spinothalamic fibers crossing in the ventral white commissure. Dorsal column (vibration, cuneate fasciculus) is spared.

h: Sjogren syndrome: characteristic antibodies?
p: Sicca syndrome (dry eyes and mouth) with anti-Ro/La. Anti-CCP is rheumatoid arthritis; anti-Scl-70 is diffuse systemic sclerosis.

h: Slurred speech, confusion, positive breathalyzer: expected sign?
p: Acute alcohol intoxication causes cerebellar-type signs (ataxia, slurred speech). Pinpoint pupils suggest opioids; vertical nystagmus suggests PCP or brainstem lesions.

h: Graves disease: process unique to it versus Hashimoto?
p: TSH-receptor antibodies also act on orbital fibroblasts and pretibial skin, causing ophthalmopathy and myxedema. Thyroid destruction is Hashimoto; high LDL is hypothyroidism.

h: Giant platelets, low count, no aggregation with ristocetin: diagnosis?
p: GpIb deficiency impairs platelet adhesion to vWF: large platelets, thrombocytopenia, ristocetin non-response that is not corrected by normal plasma. Glanzmann (GpIIb/IIIa) fails ADP aggregation with normal ristocetin response.

h: Serotonin neurons of the brainstem sit in which nuclei?
p: Raphe nuclei make serotonin (targets of SSRIs, trazodone). Locus ceruleus makes norepinephrine; substantia nigra makes dopamine.

h: Primary amenorrhea, Tanner 5, nausea and breast tenderness: first test?
p: Always exclude pregnancy first in a patient with amenorrhea and compatible symptoms, even when menarche has not occurred.

h: Anxious patient self-escalating her prescribed dose for effect: likely drug?
p: Benzodiazepines (triazolam) cause tolerance and dependence with dose escalation. Buspirone and hydroxyzine are non-addictive anxiolytics.

h: Blistering on sun-exposed skin, dark urine: defective enzyme?
p: Porphyria cutanea tarda, the most common porphyria: photosensitive blisters on hands and face, associated with hepatitis C, alcohol and iron overload.

h: Diabetes plus restrictive heart failure with preserved EF: underlying cause?
p: Hereditary hemochromatosis (HFE) deposits iron in pancreas (diabetes), heart (restrictive cardiomyopathy), liver and skin. Wilson disease is the copper disorder.

h: Rose gardener with spreading lymphocutaneous lesions: treatment?
p: Sporothrix schenckii enters via thorn pricks; lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis is treated with itraconazole (potassium iodide is an older alternative).

h: Kidney graft weeks later: endothelialitis and interstitial mononuclear cells; mediator?
p: Acute cellular rejection is T-cell mediated and appears weeks to months later. Hyperacute rejection is from preformed antibodies, within minutes to hours.

h: Child with sickle cell disease: unconjugated pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine?
p: Asplenia and sickle cell patients need PPSV23 from age 2 in addition to conjugate vaccine. Hib is a protein-conjugated vaccine; LAIV is live and not the pneumococcal one.

h: Untreated Lyme disease: which cranial nerve is classically palsied?
p: Early disseminated Lyme causes facial nerve palsy (can be bilateral), meningitis and AV block; late disease causes arthritis.

h: Infant with hepatosplenomegaly, cherry-red macula, foamy histiocytes: diagnosis?
p: Sphingomyelinase deficiency: hepatosplenomegaly, neurodegeneration, cherry-red spot. Tay-Sachs has a cherry-red spot without hepatosplenomegaly; Gaucher has no cherry-red spot.

h: Pure motor hemiparesis from internal capsule infarct: vessel pathology?
p: Lacunar strokes arise from small-vessel lipohyalinosis driven by hypertension and diabetes; typical syndromes are pure motor, pure sensory, ataxic hemiparesis.
